subject: Aurelia Health — MSA security exhibit: proposed audit bands & rolling evidence windows
messages:
From: James Carter <j.carter@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Legal <legal@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MSA security exhibit — clarification on audit windows and evidence cadence

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for sending the draft exhibit. Two specific asks from our side before legal redlines:
1) We need clear language on how audit rights are exercised — specifically a notice window for pen tests and what you consider "rolling" evidence requests (weekly snapshots vs ad-hoc).
2) Can you confirm the maximum number of inspection days per 12-month period and whether sampling will be used?

Attached is a short list of our internal evidence types for reference. We're trying to map to your SOC 2 scope to avoid repeat asks.

Appreciate a quick proposal on cadence and any proposed MSA text we can review.

Thanks,
James Carter
Head of InfoSec Programs
Aurelia Health
Attachment: aurelia_evidence_list.pdf (PDF)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: James Carter <j.carter@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — clarification on audit windows and evidence cadence

James — thanks, got the list. Quick proposal below; attaching a working redline and a one-page schedule.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Notice windows: 10 business days for scheduled SOC2 evidence requests and 15 business days for coordinated penetration test dates (we'll provide a 3-business-day confirmation window once you propose exact dates).
- Inspection days: up to 5 inspection days (combined) per 12-month period for manual review or privileged inspection; additional days require an escalation and commercial agreement.
- Evidence cadence: "rolling weekly snapshots" — we will provide a weekly bundle of SOC2-aligned artifacts (logs, configuration exports, change records) on a read-only drive link for a 4-week window after request. Ad-hoc requests limited to one per quarter unless in response to a security incident.
- Sampling: agreed — evidence will be sampled across environments and time ranges; sample selection will be coordinated and documented.

Proposed MSA snippet for the exhibit (you can paste into the draft):
"Customer may request inspection or audit rights subject to the following: (i) Customer shall provide Provider at least ten (10) business days' prior notice for scheduled documentation requests and fifteen (15) business days' prior notice for penetration-testing activities; (ii) Provider will make available up to five (5) combined inspection days per twelve (12) month period for on-site or remote privileged inspection; (iii) Provider will deliver rolling weekly artifact snapshots for up to four (4) weeks following a documented request; (iv) Ad-hoc requests are limited to one (1) per fiscal quarter unless agreed in writing or required due to a confirmed security incident; (v) Sampling methodology will be mutually agreed and documented in the evidence log."

Attachments: msaredline_v1.docx, evidence_windows_v1.xlsx

If that aligns we'll route to legal for redline, and Laura can confirm on the inspection day carve-outs (particularly around privileged access).

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, James Carter <j.carter@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:38:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — clarification on audit windows and evidence cadence

Thanks Rohan — I reviewed the snippet and have a few legal clarifications we should propose to Aurelia before sign: 
- Limit scope to production environments listed in the Order Form (explicit environment carve-out).
- Replace "on-site" with "on-site or remote with mutually agreed controls" and require Aurelia to use dedicated test accounts/ephemeral credentials for any privileged access.
- Add commercial cap language for additional inspection days beyond the five-day allowance (so we don't accept open-ended manual work).
- Confirm we are not required to produce raw logs containing PII; we will provide redacted or aggregated exports per SOC2 policy.

Suggested redline additions: 
"Provider shall not be required to provide raw audit logs containing end-user personal data; where possible, Provider will provide redacted or aggregate artifacts. Any additional inspection days beyond the five (5) day allowance shall be subject to Provider's standard professional services rates and mutual scheduling."

I'll attach a tracked-change version after internal sign-off. Olga, can you comment on pen-test operational items (staging window, service-impact guardrails)?

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, James Carter <j.carter@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — clarification on audit windows and evidence cadence

Quick ops notes from infra/ops: 
- Pen test windows: we can support a maximum 3-day staging window (non-production) and a single 24-hour production smoke test with prior approval; production penetration testing requires a runbook and an agreed out-of-band contact list.
- Credentials: we will issue ephemeral SSH keys or scoped API tokens that expire within the test window. No standing privileged accounts will be provided.
- Traffic impacts: any tests that materially increase CPU/GPU consumption beyond baseline must be scheduled with 7 business days' notice and may be refused for safety.

Operational handoff checklist (we can include as annex):
- Proposed test dates and scope
- Test harness and expected traffic profile
- Escalation contacts (ops, on-call)
- Post-test evidence package (findings, logs, remediation timeline)

We'll add a short ops annex to msaredline_v1.docx and circulate.

Olga Petrov
Head of Production Security | Redwood Inference

From: James Carter <j.carter@aureliahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — clarification on audit windows and evidence cadence

Laura/Olga/Rohan — this looks reasonable and aligned with our internal risk appetite. A few small asks before I send to Aurelia Legal for confirmation: 
- Can you add explicit language allowing us to request a log export in a redacted form within the rolling weekly snapshot? Example sentence: "Customer may request redacted log exports as part of the rolling weekly snapshots; Provider will use reasonable efforts to redact PII prior to delivery."
- For sampling, please add that the customer may request the sampling rationale in writing (we want traceability).

If you approve these two small clarifications I'll circulate to our Legal and aim to return a redline within 48 hours.

Thanks,
James
Head of InfoSec Programs | Aurelia Health
